title: Notte e giorno faticar
subtitle: Leporello, Donna Anna, Don Giovanni and the Commendatore: introduction from Don Giovanni, Act 1 (No. 1)

passages.label: Notte e giorno faticar … ed io far la sentinella!
Voglio far il gentiluomo (again) · Ma mi par che venga gente
Non sperar, se non m'uccidi · Donna folle! · Gente! servi!
Come furia disperata · Questa furia disperata · Sta a veder che il libertino
Lasciala, indegno! · Così pretendi da me fuggir? · Misero! attendi (the duel)
Andante: Ah! soccorso! son tradito! (the Commendatore's death, to the end)

licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the sung lines and the piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, then checked bar by bar and checked again by fresh checkers, whose three findings were corrected. The English singing translation and the stage directions are left out. In the opera the Overture runs straight into this number; bar 1 is the printed two-beat upbeat bar. Molto allegro 4/4 to bar 176, then Andante in cut time from bar 177 to the end. A slur joining chords in bars 36–37 cannot be shown in this format. Playback tempo: Molto allegro ♩ = 156 and Andante ♩ = 52, about 5:53 in all, from the median of five complete recordings (Fricsay 1958 5:20, Giulini 1959 5:01, Klemperer 1966 6:31, Böhm 1977 6:01, Karajan 1985 5:54; median 5:54). The tracks are not split at the Andante, so the two sections keep a set proportion: the Andante's triplet eighths move at the speed of the Molto allegro's quarter notes (Andante ♩ = a third of the Molto allegro's), the proportion that the recordings split at the duel and at the Commendatore's death suggest. Mozart gives the words Molto allegro and Andante only.
